definition: A mathematical structure consisting of a collection of objects and a collection of morphisms (arrows) between objects, equipped with an associative composition operation and an identity morphism for each object. Fundamental examples: Set (sets and functions), Grp (groups and homomorphisms), Top (topological spaces and continuous maps).
connective_patterns: objects and morphisms of a category

definition: A structure-preserving map between categories. A (covariant) functor F: C → D assigns to each object A in C an object F(A) in D, and to each morphism f: A → B a morphism F(f): F(A) → F(B), preserving identity morphisms and composition: F(id_A) = id_{F(A)} and F(g∘f) = F(g)∘F(f). A contravariant functor reverses the direction of morphisms.

A family of morphisms providing a way of transforming one functor into another while respecting the internal structure of the categories involved. Given functors F, G: C → D, a natural transformation η: F ⇒ G assigns to each object A in C a morphism η_A: F(A) → G(A) such that for every morphism f: A → B, the naturality square commutes: η_B ∘ F(f) = G(f) ∘ η_A. Natural transformations are 'morphisms of functors'.

A relationship between two functors F: C → D and G: D → C (written F ⊣ G) given by a natural bijection Hom_D(FA, B) ≅ Hom_C(A, GB) for all objects A in C and B in D. F is the left adjoint and G is the right adjoint. Every adjunction gives rise to a unit η: Id_C ⇒ GF and counit ε: FG ⇒ Id_D. Adjunctions are ubiquitous: free/forgetful, tensor/hom, sheafification/inclusion.
connective_patterns: F is left adjoint to G

definition: An arrow between two objects in a category, generalizing the notion of structure-preserving map. Morphisms compose associatively and each object has an identity morphism. Specific instances: homomorphisms (groups), continuous maps (spaces), linear maps (vector spaces). A morphism is not required to be a function—it is an abstract arrow satisfying the category axioms.

A morphism f: A → B in a category that has a two-sided inverse: there exists g: B → A such that g∘f = id_A and f∘g = id_B. Isomorphic objects are structurally identical from the category's perspective. An isomorphism in Set is a bijection; in Grp, a group isomorphism; in Top, a homeomorphism.

An equivalence of categories is a functor F: C → D for which there exists a functor G: D → C and natural isomorphisms GF ≅ Id_C and FG ≅ Id_D. Weaker than isomorphism of categories (which requires GF = Id and FG = Id on the nose) but captures the right notion of 'sameness' for categories, since categories form a 2-category.

A universal construction in a category that generalizes products, equalizers, pullbacks, and inverse limits. Given a diagram D: J → C (a functor from an index category J), the limit lim D is an object L with morphisms to each D(j) satisfying a universal property: any other cone over D factors uniquely through L. Dually, the colimit is the universal cocone.

The dual of a limit. Given a diagram D: J → C, the colimit colim D is an object L with morphisms from each D(j) to L satisfying the universal property: any other cocone under D factors uniquely through L. Colimits generalize coproducts, coequalizers, pushouts, and direct limits.

A triple (T, η, μ) consisting of an endofunctor T: C → C and two natural transformations—unit η: Id_C ⇒ T and multiplication μ: T² ⇒ T—satisfying associativity (μ ∘ Tμ = μ ∘ μT) and unit laws (μ ∘ Tη = μ ∘ ηT = id_T). Equivalently, a monoid in the category of endofunctors. Every adjunction F ⊣ G gives rise to a monad GF on C. Monads encode algebraic theories and computational effects.

A contravariant functor F: C^op → Set from a category C to the category of sets. The category of presheaves [C^op, Set] is a fundamental construction: it is a topos (has all limits, colimits, and an internal logic). The Yoneda embedding y: C → [C^op, Set] sends each object A to the representable presheaf Hom(-, A). Every presheaf is a colimit of representables (density theorem).

A presheaf on a site (a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology) that satisfies a gluing condition: local data that agree on overlaps can be uniquely glued to global data. Sheaves generalize the notion of 'functions defined locally that patch together globally'. The category of sheaves on a site is a Grothendieck topos.

For a locally small category C, the Yoneda lemma states: Nat(Hom_C(A, -), F) ≅ F(A) for every functor F: C → Set and object A in C. The bijection is natural in both A and F. Consequence: the Yoneda embedding y: C → [C^op, Set] defined by y(A) = Hom(-, A) is fully faithful—C embeds into its presheaf category preserving all information about morphisms. Often described as 'an object is completely determined by its relationships to all other objects'.
connective_patterns: an object is determined by its hom-functor

definition: The fundamental operation in a category: given morphisms f: A → B and g: B → C, their composition g∘f: A → C is a morphism from A to C. Composition must be associative: h∘(g∘f) = (h∘g)∘f. Together with identity morphisms, composition defines the structure of a category.

For each object A in a category, the identity morphism id_A: A → A is the unique morphism satisfying f∘id_A = f and id_A∘g = g for all morphisms f: A → B and g: C → A. The existence of identity morphisms is one of the axioms defining a category.
